name: Cuprum Metallicum
origin: Metallic copper obtained from copper ores and native copper deposits
habitat: Found native and in copper ores worldwide
preparation: Trituration of pure metallic copper, followed by successive attenuations
chemicalConstituents: Copper (Cu), essentially pure in the homeopathic preparation
generalAnalysis: A mineral remedy whose traditional picture is dominated by violent, spasmodic and convulsive phenomena. Cramps and convulsions classically begin in the fingers and toes and spread centrally, with blueness and coldness of the surface, intense nausea, and a striking amelioration from drinking cold water.

drugPicture.generalPicture: A picture of violent spasm. The patient is seized by cramps or convulsions that begin in the extremities, with piercing cries, a bluish or livid face, cold hands and intense nausea. The attacks recur periodically and in groups, and a swallow of cold water often brings relief.

differences: Belladonna has a hot, red face and dilated pupils; Cuprum has a cold, blue or livid face
Belladonna is worse from light, noise and jarring
Cuprum spasms often begin in the fingers and toes with clenched thumbs
Cicuta features opisthotonos and marked head retraction
Cuprum is more often associated with peripheral onset and cyanosis
The Cuprum picture includes intense nausea and relief from cold water
Veratrum album has profuse watery diarrhoea and vomiting with icy coldness
Cuprum is dominated by spasms and convulsions rather than fluid loss
Cuprum has the characteristic metallic taste and cold-water amelioration
